cohorts.title: Cohorts

schedule.title: Requirement dates
schedule.subtitleNew: Each module gets a default completion deadline (the cohort end date unless you choose another). Once the cohort is saved, every required unit has its own date.
schedule.subtitleSaved: One date per required unit — one per selected week for Training. Learner, Sponsor and Admin progress, overdue and checkpoints all use exactly these dates.
schedule.datesChangedNote: Changing the cohort dates moves only the defaults still set to the cohort end date, and the requirements that follow them. A date you chose stays where you put it.
schedule.loadError: The requirement schedule could not be loaded.
schedule.needProgrammeAndDates: Choose a programme, start date and end date to see the proposed deadlines.
schedule.empty: No completion deadlines are set for this cohort.
schedule.trainingNote: A Training week starts at its pacing date (cohort week date, else cohort start + week). Give a week its own date to move it; it then affects due, overdue and checkpoints like any other requirement.

issues.surplus_dates: {{module}}: {{scheduled}} units exist but only {{required}} are required — the extra ones already carry activity and were kept.
issues.outside_cohort: {{module}}: a date falls outside the cohort dates.
issues.out_of_scope: {{module}}: dates exist but the module is no longer required by the programme.
issues.missing_deadline: {{module}}: no completion deadline is set, so no requirement can be created.

schedule.unitsNote: The programme sets how many units each module requires; the cohort holds exactly one dated requirement per unit.
schedule.countMismatch: {{required}} units are required but {{scheduled}} requirements exist.
schedule.newCohortNote: Individual requirement dates (one per required unit, one per Training week) can be edited once the cohort is saved.

integrity.training_units_mismatch: Training: {{detail}} — the programme should select exactly one week per required unit.

integrity.schedule_out_of_scope: {{module}}: requirements exist but the module is no longer required ({{detail}}).
